frase_gancho.texto: Heirs of the maguey and the living fiber that sustain faith on the plateau.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: This gallery is dedicated to the great Otopame language family, made up of the Otomí, Mazahua, Matlatzinca, Tlahuica, Pame, and Chichimec Jonaz peoples. Spread across the valleys and mountain ranges of the Central Highlands, these peoples have shown extraordinary adaptability in the face of semiarid environments and historical change. The tour presents the full use of the maguey to obtain pulque and ixtle fibers, backstrap loom weaving with intricate geometric designs, and carvings inlaid with shell. It also brings to light the devotion expressed in family oratories and the communal fervor of their patron saint ceremonies and the agricultural cycle.
